name: Sightlines and Camera Tricks
description: A special training ground has been set up in the southern section of Lumidouce Harbor in Fontaine...

dialogs.content: ...Terminal ballistics are impeccable, and the dispersion is close to the ideal.
According to our assessment models here at the Maison Gardiennage's weapons bureau, your weapon is very much a "cannon."
It's just a shame that we'd need at least two teams' worth of manpower to deploy your "musket" in the field. It's too complicated to use...
Thank you for the approval, Officer Chevreuse. Actually, I don't think the high barrier to entry's a bad thing. Before I had the "Soulsniper: Ritual Staff" custom-made by Xilonen, we agreed that...
"The stronger the weapon, the stricter its usage standards should be."
Apart from their difficulty of use, I've even considered placing a "moral cognition-based lock" on such weapons.
That way, we can ensure they are wielded by the right people, preventing any immense damage resulting from criminal theft.
That's a fair concern, Officer Chasca. Weapon theft that leads to committed crimes is not uncommon here in Fontaine.
Wow, so many old friends!
Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan"... and a Knight of Favonius? What's going on with this little gathering of yours?
Reconvening the multilateral exchange?
Another joint wargame?
#Bullseye. You caught on to the situation immediately, {NICKNAME}.

Some time back, the Special Patrol sent Turenna to Liyue to take part in a joint wargame. That wargame became the catalyst for ever more frequent exchanges between the armed forces of various nations.
This time around, it's the routine "Ballistic Wargame" between Fontaine and Mondstadt — aimed at sharpening combatants' battlefield-planning capabilities on all sides.
And this time, thanks to our friends in the Knights of Favonius putting in a good word, the warriors of Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan" have joined the wargame as well.
The Flower-Feather Clan warriors are skilled at firing while in flight — they've opened the doors to a whole new world for us!
Hmm... The Knights must have gotten to know the Natlanese warriors during their expedition, then? Paimon should've thought of that sooner!
But what's a "Ballistic Wargame," really? Paimon understands every word individually, but put them together and it gets a little confusing...
Doesn't shooting just mean firing the gun and being done with it?
Are bullets allowed in wargames too?
Aha, if everyone had unlimited ammunition, you'd just hold down the trigger, and most enemies would be no problem at all.
But combat is a long-drawn-out process. A shooter can only carry so much ammunition, so every shot needs to land — and to land strategically.
So the Knights of Favonius have developed a new type of grenade to help shooters sharpen their understanding. The principle behind it is a little complicated, though...
As for the specifics, I'll let our friend from the Knights of Favonius walk you through it.
#Coming, coming — apologies! I was buried in report-organizing and hadn't even noticed the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} little white companion. My greetings to you both!
I'm Hedwig, member of the Knights of Favonius's General Affairs Company. I'm in charge of recording proceedings for this wargame, and coordinating between the gunsmiths and our other allies...
Speaking of which — the device for this round actually has a connection to you two. Do you remember the strange Samachurl statue that once appeared in Dadaupa Gorge?
Vaguely. Long time ago, that.
Don't remember. Doesn't matter, does it?
Even Paimon's a bit fuzzy on it. Hedwig, why don't you give us the short version?
Right then. I'll skip past the old legends and the scattered intel and cut to it —

According to the Investigation Company's findings, that statue was the work of an ancient Samachurl. The "Ladler of Broth" Churldric had taken an unused Domain and reshaped it into a place to drill his battle formations.
The Honorary Knight defeated one of Churldric's lingering shadows back then, which caused the Domain to collapse — and the "Eyes of Upano" that oversaw the formations scattered out into the open.

Once the Support Company had a sample in hand, they spent the better part of a year carefully disassembling and analyzing it. Eventually they got the technology figured out, combined it with the design principles of Liyue's overhead surveillance devices...
...And produced a kind of visualizing "observation grenade" — meant for long-range reconnaissance, so a shooter can gather information from a position of safety.
What a roundabout journey... Paimon never imagined that little fellow we wrapped up without much fanfare would leave behind such a mysterious treasure!
The upshot is, in a wargame setting, the "observation grenade" lets shooters see through the eyes of the round in flight — deepening their grasp of trajectory and obstacles...
...So they can practice shooting strategies geared toward different scenarios. It works on quite a few clever little angles!

As for us Flower-Feather Clan members, our Saurian-riders often have difficulty determining the effects of shots we make while riding our Qucusaurs. We are up in the sky, after all, with our targets being far away...
These observation grenades can thus help us conduct battlefield damage assessments... That's a term I learned from the Special Patrol, by the by — it's a very concise concept.
Sounds pretty neat.
At present, the people involved in the wargame have completed everything our two leaders, Chasca and Chevreuse, have designated for them.
All that's left is to complete our wargame with an expanded sample.
Since you're here, Honorary Knight, would you like to try it out?
By all means!
I did notice during the Fontinalia Film Festival that you're quite a crack shot, and an inspired one, too.
That's perfect.
#I'm personally interested to see how much your marksmanship's improved over the years, {NICKNAME}.
And from the perspective of the wargame, your lack of familiarity with the observation grenades means that you can form an excellent control group for us.
#Heh. Y'know, {NICKNAME}... It does feel like this grenade thing has real history with us.
Might as well try its effects for ourselves, eh? It should be pretty fun!
Guess I'll have to step up and take this seriously.
Totally! An extra skill's an extra skill, right? Never know if we'll run into some sorta... bad guy who can only be taken out with muskets or something!
Great! In that case, I'll prepare the venue and notify all those we have playing as targets!
The rules are simple: Make as few "adjustments" as possible while defeating your targets efficiently...
I should first say that this drill was made to be tough. Even the Special Patrol's previous marksmanship instructor, Enghiene, was barely able to pass...
But I suspect you'll do just fine.

Of course, there's no need to feel pressured. Sometimes, shooting is not just about technique, but also about inspiration that arrives as light as feathers, and a little luck to send it off on the wind.
Don't think of this as a test, but more as a relaxing game. Perhaps you'll gain something unexpected from all this, hmm?
A bit of marksmanship practice is good for me too.
Glad to be of help.
